pages.contents: One landscape slide titled as a longitudinal clinical course of a patient with blue rubber bleb nevus syndrome. A horizontal timeline marks 18 months, 7 years, 9–12 years, 15 years, 17 years and 20 years; under each marker four labelled blocks (presentation, assessment, treatment, outcome) hold one or two lines of text. A lower shaded band is headed follow-up after discharge (age 20 years) with markers at 2 weeks, 1 month and 2 months and a short statement at each, plus a statement of early improvement and that longer follow-up is required. The page is text and vector graphics without embedded images.
pages.clinical_relevance_notes: The page restates the age-based course in Table 1 of the article for the single index patient (the article cites it as Supplementary Data sheet 1) and adds the 2-week, 1-month and 2-month follow-up statements also given in the text. It names the 9–12 year block as one column, whereas Table 1 lists 9 and 12 years separately; the page does not state the same events differently. Typed facts transcribe the printed text only.
limitations: No license notice, logo or copyright text is printed on the page; the main article license is provenance, not blanket asset licensing.

transcriptions.text: Longitudinal clinical course of a patient with blue rubber bleb nevus syndrome
Bluish-purple cutaneous and soft-tissue venous malformations
Blood transfusion; resection of small-intestinal, colonic, and superficial lesions
Worsening hematochezia, palpitations, and fatigue; Hb 34 g/L
CBC, gastroscopy, colonoscopy, and pelvic MRI
Endoscopic sclerotherapy of gastric and duodenal lesions; open excision of multiple intestinal venous malformations
Uneventful recovery; gastrointestinal bleeding and anemia improved
Recurrent melena and fatigue for 2 months; extensive superficial and soft-tissue venous malformations; Hb 55 g/L
Vital signs, physical examination, and CBC
Packed red-cell transfusion, oral hematinic and hemostatic therapy, and percutaneous lauromacrogol sclerotherapy
Hb 98 g/L at discharge; clinically stable; no documented complications
longer follow-up is required to determine whether disease control is durable.
No recurrent melena or hematochezia; no transfusion
No recurrent bleeding; continued oral iron supplementation
No recurrent bleeding or further transfusion; Hb 113 g/L; no complications
